answer: A marketplace can require each agent to stake a refundable deposit and complete a slow, verifiable history of useful trades before it earns full trust, like crossing a canyon on a single narrow bridge rather than flooding a meadow with copies. New identities start on a mesa with tiny limits: one listing, delayed settlement, and peer review. Creating thousands of clones then costs real capital locked for weeks plus the time to build distinct reputations, while one honest agent passes cheaply.
